questions.prompt: What does `std::move(x)` actually do at runtime when executed on a local `std::vector<int> x`?
options: std::move copies the heap pointer and zeroes a inside the std::move function body
std::move emits zero instructions; it simply casts a to an xvalue so vector's move constructor is selected
std::move immediately invokes a.~vector() after returning
std::move swaps the stack frames of a and b
questions.explanation: std::move is a pure compile-time cast to std::remove_reference_t<T>&& ([utility.move]). The actual pointer transfer and zeroing happen inside std::vector's move constructor because overload resolution picks vector(vector&&) for the xvalue.

questions.prompt: What happens when you initialize `b` using `const std::string a = "hello"; std::string b = std::move(a);`?
questions.code:
const std::string a = "hello";
std::string b = std::move(a);
options: Compilation fails because you cannot pass a const object to std::move
std::string's move constructor runs and clears a
std::string's copy constructor runs because std::move(a) has type const std::string&&
Undefined behavior from modifying a const object
questions.explanation: std::move(a) preserves constness and returns const std::string&&. Because std::string(std::string&&) requires a non-const rvalue reference, overload resolution selects std::string(const std::string&) and copies a.

questions.prompt: Why does `std::vector<Item>::push_back` copy existing `Item` elements during reallocation when `Item` declares both `Item(const Item&)` and `Item(Item&&)` without `noexcept`?
options: std::vector never moves elements during reallocation; it always copies
std::vector uses std::move_if_noexcept, which falls back to copying so the old buffer stays intact if moving throws mid-reallocation
Non-noexcept move constructors are treated as deleted by std::allocator
Because Item lacks a user-declared destructor, its move constructor is suppressed
questions.explanation: To preserve push_back's strong exception guarantee, std::vector calls std::move_if_noexcept ([utility.move.if.noexcept]). Because Item has a copy constructor and its move constructor is not noexcept, move_if_noexcept yields const Item& and copies safely.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of adding `~Widget() = default;` to a struct that has a `std::string` member and no explicitly declared copy or move functions?
options: Both copy and move operations remain implicitly defaulted as before
Copy operations are deleted while move operations remain defaulted
Move constructor and move assignment are implicitly deleted
Implicit move constructor and move assignment are not declared (suppressed), so moving Widget silently calls its copy operations
questions.explanation: Under [class.copy.ctor] and [class.copy.assign], any user-declared destructor suppresses implicit declaration of both the move constructor and move assignment operator. Implicit copy operations remain declared, so moves quietly degrade into copies.

questions.prompt: What does the C++ standard guarantee about a moved-from `std::string s` after `auto t = std::move(s);`?
options: s is in a valid but unspecified state: it can be safely destroyed or reassigned, though its contents and length are unspecified
s is guaranteed to have s.empty() == true and s.capacity() == 0
Using s in any way—including destruction—is undefined behavior
s retains its original characters until s goes out of scope
questions.explanation: [lib.types.movedfrom] specifies that moved-from standard library objects are placed in a valid but unspecified state unless explicitly specified otherwise. Calling clear() or assigning a new value is safe; assuming empty() is not.

questions.prompt: Why does `Output finalize(Builder b) { return b; }` compile in C++23 when `Builder` defines only `operator Output() &&` and deletes `operator Output() const&`?
options: NRVO eliminates the conversion operator entirely for function parameters
C++23 P2266R3 classifies b in return b as move-eligible, so overload resolution treats b as an rvalue during implicit move
Parameters passed by value are always prvalues inside the function body
Because operator Output() const& is deleted, the compiler calls reinterpret_cast
questions.explanation: Under C++23 [class.copy.elision] (P2266R3), an id-expression naming an automatic variable or parameter in a return statement is move-eligible, triggering an rvalue-first overload lookup that picks operator Output() && without needing std::move(b).
